chunks: Ahmad b. al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: al-Abbas b. al-Fadl al-Muqri' narrated to us. He said: Abu'l Hasan Ali b. al-Furat al-Isfahani narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad al-Basri narrated to us. He said: Jundal b. Waliq narrated to us. He said: Ali b. Hammad narrated to us from Sa'id from Ibn Abbas.

He passed by a gathering of Quraysh that was insulting Ali b. Abi Talib (as), so he said to his guide: What are these people saying? He said: They are insulting Ali. He said: Bring me closer to them. When he reached them, he said: Which of you insulted Allah? They said: Glory be to Allah! Whoever insults Allah has associated partners with Him. He said: Then which of you insulted the Messenger of Allah (s)? They said: Whoever insults the Messenger of Allah has disbelieved. He said: Then which of you insulted Ali b. Abi Talib? They said: That indeed happened. He said: I testify by Allah and I testify for Allah that I heard the Messenger of Allah (s) say: Whoever insults Ali has insulted me, and whoever insults me has insulted Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

Then he went on. He said to his guide: Did they say anything when I said what I said to them? He said: They did not say anything. He said: How did you see their faces? He said: They looked at you with reddened eyes, as a goat looks to the knife of a butcher. He said: Tell me more, may your father be your ransom.

He said: Squinting eyes and furrowed brows, lowered chins in humiliation — the look of a servile man to a glorious and dominant man. He said: Tell me more, may your father be your ransom. He said: I have nothing more. He said: But I have: Their living ones are a disgrace to their dead, and their dead are a shame for the ancients.

key_terms.أَشْرَكَ: To commit shirk – associating partners with God
key_terms.سَبَّ: To insult/revile – a grave act in Islamic ethics
key_terms.قَائِد: Guide – one who leads a blind person

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about insulting Imam Ali according to Ibn Abbas?
ai.summary: Ibn Abbas, the Prophet’s cousin and a renowned companion, passed by a gathering of Quraysh who were insulting Imam Ali (as). Being blind, he asked his guide what they were saying, then systematically confronted them: insulting God is shirk, insulting the Prophet is disbelief, so what of insulting Ali? He quoted the Prophet’s saying that insulting Ali is equivalent to insulting the Prophet, which is equivalent to insulting God. The narration concludes with a poetic exchange describing the humiliated expressions of the Quraysh.
